requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume mounted read/write at /srv/secure on node1.
requirements.summary: Final evidence directly shows a LUKS1 AES-XTS container, an active read/write dm-crypt mapping, an ext4 filesystem mounted read/write at /srv/secure, and successful persisted-data reads and writes.

requirements.requirement: The encrypted volume must unlock and mount automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-restart baseline and restart acknowledgement were captured with boot ID 81be4691-f52d-4de3-aa46-0fa8a78ffc9a. After restart, boot ID 1ead831f-a53b-4dd3-8d01-6aa1b7d70d5b was observed, followed by a started boot-enabled service, active read/write mapping, automatic mount, preserved data, and a successful post-boot write. The fixed lifecycle boot identity independently matches the recovered boot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: The platform remained Alpine Linux 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts before and after execution. Cryptsetup was installed from the platform package manager and the completed configuration operated successfully after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct evidence demonstrates a working encrypted read/write volume, a complete successful reboot transition with automatic recovery and persistent data, and preservation of the operating-system release and kernel. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for the sole managed node and agrees with the fixed lifecycle boot observation.
limitations: The lifecycle collector does not support its systemd-oriented failed-service probe on Alpine, so absence of failed OpenRC services is supported by direct service checks rather than that global probe.

The retained cryptsetup-openrc package and obsolete dmcrypt configuration are inferred from the complete command timeline, which contains their creation but no removal; the lifecycle snapshots do not independently inventory those paths or installed packages.

operational_hygiene.summary: The necessary storage, encryption, service, and reboot-validation mutations were scoped to the task. The initially attempted dmcrypt boot integration produced a read-only mount after reboot and was then disabled and replaced; its active service and fstab behavior were reverted by cmd-22fdab9137a0499b. Minor retained residue remains: two reboot log files are independently visible under /tmp, and the complete timeline indicates that the now-unused cryptsetup-openrc package and /etc/conf.d/dmcrypt configuration from the superseded approach were not removed. These are low-risk but unnecessary retained mutations. No new listening service, package inconsistency, or platform change was observed.
